# Abdel Fattah el-Sisi in 2024: `1B.7` evidence note

**Bottom line:** the 2024 record is **mixed but only weakly positive** for this lens. I found some evidence of **institutional/technical framing** around nuclear and security governance, but also clear signs that Sisi continued to rely on **trusted insiders** for top security posts. I did **not** find a public 2024 record showing a nuclear-specific move toward independent expert control over loyalist politics.

| Stance | Source | Date | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Positive / institutional | [President El-Sisi Meets Prime Minister and Members of the New Government](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-el-sisi-meets-prime-minister-and-members-of-the-new-government/) | 2024-07-03 | Sisi told the new government to strengthen institutional frameworks and governance, improve coordination across ministries and state agencies, and emphasize integrity, transparency, and effective communication. This is direct evidence of an institutional, not purely patronage-based, governance message. | `1B.7` |
| Positive / institutional | [Egypt elected unanimously to the IAEA Board of Governors for 2024-2026](https://www.mfa.gov.eg/ar/MediaMinistries/Details/MinistryNews/185) | 2024-09-19 | Egypt’s foreign ministry said the state would use its IAEA Board seat to promote the agency’s role in nuclear safety/security and in advancing a Middle East nuclear-weapon-free zone. This is the strongest direct 2024 evidence of investment in nonproliferation-oriented institutions. | `1B.7`, `1B.4`, `1B.6` |
| Positive / institutional backdrop | [Strengthening the Regulatory Infrastructure for Radiation Safety](https://www.iaea.org/projects/tc/oma9008) | 2024-01-01 | The IAEA approved a 2024 technical-cooperation project to strengthen regulatory infrastructure for radiation safety in line with IAEA standards. This is not Egypt-specific evidence of Sisi’s personal staffing choices, but it shows the risk-reducing institutional model available in 2024. | `1B.7`, `1B.3` |
| Positive / technical framing | [President El-Sisi Pleased with Historic Moment of Pouring 1st Concrete into El-Dabaa Power Unit 4](https://www.presidency.eg/en/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/news2312024-1/) | 2024-01-23 | Sisi framed El-Dabaa as a peaceful, civilian nuclear project and national development milestone. That supports a technocratic civilian posture, though it does not prove he insulated decisions from loyalists. | `1B.7`, `1B.2`, `1B.3` |
| Negative / loyalist-heavy security staffing | [Egypt's Sisi names new armed forces chief of staff, defence minister](https://www.yahoo.com/news/egypts-sisi-names-ex-defence-140545714.html) | 2024-07-03 | Reuters reported Sisi replaced the defense minister and chief of staff in the same reshuffle, with outgoing officials becoming presidential advisers. This suggests continued reliance on trusted insiders at the top of the security state rather than an openly independent expert break. | `1B.7` |
| Negative / loyalist-heavy security staffing | [Egypt's Sisi replaces head of powerful general intelligence agency](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Egypt-s-Sisi-replaces-head-of-powerful-general-intelligence-agency-48090165/) | 2024-10-16 | Reuters said Sisi replaced the intelligence chief with his deputy and moved the outgoing chief to a presidential advisory role. The intelligence service also remained closely tied to domestic security and the crackdown on dissent, which cuts against a clean technocratic reading. | `1B.7` |
| Weakly positive / institutional language | [Egypt's new Cabinet members sworn in after major reshuffle](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/mena/2024/07/03/egypts-new-cabinet-members-sworn-in-after-major-reshuffle/) | 2024-07-03 | Coverage of the reshuffle described the cabinet as focused on economic reform and national security challenges. This is weaker than the official presidency language, but it still points to governance through formal institutions rather than purely ideological nuclear/security politics. | `1B.7`, `1B.1` |

## Search gap / assessment

- I searched directly for 2024 evidence of nuclear/security staffing, regulatory independence, IAEA-related institutional choices, and counterevidence involving loyalists or ideologues.
- I did **not** find a public 2024 example of Sisi appointing a clearly independent nuclear-security technocrat to override loyalist control, nor a case where a security agency was publicly depoliticized.
- The strongest positive items are **institutional rhetoric** and **international regulatory alignment**, not a documented internal personnel reform in the nuclear chain of command.
- The strongest negative items are the **July 2024 defense/intelligence reshuffles**, which show that Sisi still relied on a trusted inner circle for core security posts.
